steps.description: Implement the bootstrap numerical experiment to probe solution space rigidity via neural network capacity. Construct a linear constraint system (rigid, unique solution) as the baseline. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with L-BFGS-B to train small feedforward networks, sweep hidden width h for varying constraint counts w, measure zero-violation status (留出误差 ≤ 1e-3), and tabulate N_c(w) trends. Ensure all errors are finite floats and include multi-seed statistics.

plans.objective: [DEFECT] The optimization landscape contains spurious local minima that trap the solver at lower widths; apparent rigidity (flat/decreasing $N_c(w)$) is an artifact of optimization failure rather than true solution space properties, as the solver cannot reach the feasible set without increased capacity to escape basins of attraction.

steps.description: The hypothesis posits that apparent rigidity in N_c(w) is an optimization artifact. The previous prediction (surprise=0.96) likely failed because the solver got trapped in local minima at low widths. To verify, I will first perform a bootstrap feasibility check (Step 0) to ensure zero-violation is reachable with the proposed L-BFGS-B optimizer and sufficient capacity. If reachable, I will run a systematic width scan (h=1 to h_max=50) across multiple constraint widths (w) and random seeds, using multi-start optimization to avoid local traps. This will produce the N_c(w) table and trend analysis needed to distinguish between true rigidity (flat/decreasing N_c) and optimization failure (increasing N_c or false flatness).
